title: Sunny and the Sugar Glider | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka watches in quiet wonder as a tiny sugar glider sails silently from tree to tree on moonlit wings of silver. A magical and calming bedtime story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories for toddlers ready for sleep.
narration:
The gum trees stood very tall in the moonlight, their trunks pale as candles, their leaves hardly stirring. Little Sunny the quokka was out for her evening walk, her paws quiet on the cool earth, her big brown eyes looking up at the stars.

Then — something moved.

High in the branches, a tiny shape unfolded its arms. For a moment it was perfectly still. Then it leapt — and flew.

Sunny gasped, very softly. The little sugar glider sailed through the air, arms and sides stretched wide, riding the moonlit night like a whisper. Not flapping. Not tumbling. Just gliding, smooth and sure, from one tall tree to the next.

Sunny watched with her mouth a perfect little 'O'. The glider landed gently on the far tree, its tiny claws gripping the bark. It turned its round eyes toward her, black and bright and shining.

Then it jumped again.

Over and over it glided between the trees, catching the soft night air, tracing long silver arcs against the deep navy sky. Sunny tilted her head back and followed every swoop, every curve, her big warm eyes wide open.

Slowly, slowly, the little glider climbed high into a hollow in the oldest gum tree and disappeared from view. The bush was quiet again. Just moonlight and stars and the faint smell of eucalyptus.

Sunny sat down in the soft grass with a happy sigh. She had never seen anything quite so graceful. She lay back, looked at the sky, and let her eyes grow heavy.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little sugar glider. Goodnight, little one.
